title: Complete fixed-resolvent rank-six locus and sharp corank-three compression loss
statement: Over every field, the rank-at-most-six locus of the fixed 112-dimensional resolvent matrix space W is a 17-dimensional linear subspace, and every nonzero member has the same six-dimensional image. Its mixed outer block has a five-dimensional rank-six locus, certified by 26 triangular seven-minors and five terminal six-minors over Z. Over an algebraically closed field, arbitrary rank109 compression factors on both sides have kernel dimension at most one on W, with the left kernel necessarily in the common six-space if loss occurs. A displayed compression attains image dimension111.
dependencies: Pinned fixed-resolvent source and minimum-rank package, AI-RESOLVENT-SHARP-MINRANK-001
Exact integer minor identities and terminal support certificate
Written quotient-space and determinant-pencil argument over algebraically closed fields
limitations: Ordinary matrix rank, not tensor slice rank. The one-dimensional compression-kernel bound assumes an algebraically closed field. Different nilpotents, higher resolvent corrections, arbitrary singular Laurent trajectories, independent mathematical review, formalization, and exponent improvement remain outside scope.

title: Fixed-resolvent rank-seven gap and all-field six-loss compression boundary
statement: Over every field the rank-at-most-seven locus of W equals its 17-dimensional rank-six space, with no rank-seven matrices; a unit minor witnesses rank eight. If the output and input coranks a,b satisfy a+b=6 and b>=1, the compression kernel has dimension at most one, sharply for all six allocations. If (a,b)=(6,0), the kernel has dimension17 exactly when the output kernel is the common six-dimensional image, and is zero otherwise. Scalar extension proves the one-dimensional bound over every field.
dependencies: AI-RESOLVENT-RANK-SIX-LOCUS-001 and its explicit common-image classification
Twenty-six triangular eight-minor identities and a unit rank-eight minor
limitations: Only the fixed resolvent matrix space W; total-loss-seven kernel dimensions and general singular Laurent trajectories are not classified. This is ordinary matrix rank, with no tensor target, independent review, formalization, or exponent improvement.
